rites.name: Kelornen
rites.text: Kelornen is the concept of the first sounding in Lernaunus, the note by which the roots of the world condensed out of silence. It is less a being than a resonance that persists as the pattern every later thing must echo.

rites.name: Kuzhournak
rites.text: Kuzhournak is a concept in Lernaunus, a principle of the Courts that the divine councils invoked when they judged trials and set the doors between worlds. In the Age of the first sovereign it was taught in the groves as the measure by which growing kingdoms were allowed to stand.

rites.name: Taunialles
rites.text: Taunialles is the concept of a threshold, the binding that holds one world's edge against another's during the Age of Sundering. In the Courts it was argued over as a principle rather than a figure, and its keeping passed from council to council as the doors between worlds were raised.

rites.name: Kelordedar
rites.text: Kelordedar is the concept of the Weave-root that the makers planted in Lernaunus during the Seeding, a quiet power that holds the sleeping powers in place. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds, it was the thread that kept the scattered powers from unraveling entirely.

rites.name: Ryirlamae
rites.text: Ryirlamae is the Walled Age's concept of a sealed flame, kept burning within the temple walls and handed from one order to the next. In the Holy Age, the faithful believed the flame could hold back the dark beyond the walls, and its keepers tested it at the thresholds of every new crossing.

rites.name: Sithora
rites.text: Sithora is a concept in Lernaunus, a idea that the Library keeps as a shelved branch of the Three Futures, where the ending splits into many paths during the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders. It is said to be the name given to the moment a single choice becomes a pillar of the Record. Its meaning shifts depending on which order is reading it.

rites.name: Veneineth
rites.text: Veneineth is a concept of Lernaunus, the idea of a branching ending kept in the Library, where every possible outcome is shelved side by side. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between peoples, it became the lens through which survivors weighed which future to pursue.
